# Problem Statement

An e-commerce company wants to understand its customers and improve marketing decisions.
Using historical online-retail transactions, this notebook (in **R**):

1. pre-processes the data and engineers customer-level features (RFM, average transaction value, quantity, purchase frequency);
2. segments customers with **K-Means** (Elbow Method) and compares with **Hierarchical Clustering** (dendrogram), validated by the **Silhouette Score**;
3. visualises segments with a **2D PCA** projection and an **interactive 3D Plotly** plot;
4. profiles every cluster;
5. builds **Random Forest** and **SVM** classifiers to predict membership of the high-value segment and compares them with Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC and Confusion Matrices;
6. analyses feature importance and recommends segment-wise marketing strategies.

# Dataset Description

**UCI Machine Learning Repository: Online Retail** (541,909 transactions of a UK-based online gift-ware retailer, 01-Dec-2010 to 09-Dec-2011).

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| InvoiceNo | Invoice number. A leading `C` marks a **cancellation** |
| StockCode | Product code |
| Description | Product name |
| Quantity | Units per line item (negative for returns) |
| InvoiceDate | Date and time of the transaction |
| UnitPrice | Price per unit in GBP |
| CustomerID | Customer identifier (about 25% missing) |
| Country | Customer's country |

```{r load-data}
# ---- Data loading ---------------------------------------------------------
# Order of attempts: (1) local xlsx, (2) local csv, (3) download from UCI,
# (4) synthetic fallback ONLY if you set Sys.setenv(USE_SYNTHETIC = "1").
xlsx_path <- "data/Online Retail.xlsx"
csv_path  <- "data/OnlineRetail.csv"
rds_path  <- "data/online_retail.rds"       # cache so later knits are fast
using_synthetic <- FALSE

if (file.exists(rds_path)) {
  raw <- readRDS(rds_path)
} else if (file.exists(xlsx_path)) {
  raw <- read_excel(xlsx_path); saveRDS(raw, rds_path)
} else if (file.exists(csv_path)) {
  raw <- read.csv(csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "latin1"); saveRDS(raw, rds_path)
} else if (Sys.getenv("USE_SYNTHETIC") == "1") {
  source("data/generate_synthetic_data.R")
  raw <- generate_synthetic_retail(); using_synthetic <- TRUE
} else {
  url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/352/online+retail.zip"
  zipf <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  ok <- tryCatch({ download.file(url, zipf, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE); TRUE },
                 error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)
  if (!ok) stop("Could not download the dataset. Download 'Online Retail.xlsx' from the UCI ",
                "repository manually and place it in the data/ folder.")
  unzip(zipf, exdir = "data")
  raw <- read_excel(xlsx_path); saveRDS(raw, rds_path)
}
raw$InvoiceDate <- as.POSIXct(raw$InvoiceDate, tz = "UTC")
raw$InvoiceNo   <- as.character(raw$InvoiceNo)
if (using_synthetic) cat("*** USING SYNTHETIC DATA (pipeline test only) ***\n")
cat("Rows:", nrow(raw), " Columns:", ncol(raw), "\n")
glimpse(raw)
summary(raw[, c("Quantity", "UnitPrice")])
```

# Data Preprocessing and Cleaning

Handling of missing values, cancellations and invalid records, with a log of rows removed at each step.

```{r cleaning}
log_step <- function(df, label, prev) data.frame(Step = label, RowsRemaining = nrow(df),
                                                RowsRemoved = prev - nrow(df))
steps <- list(); df <- raw; n0 <- nrow(df)
steps[[1]] <- data.frame(Step = "Raw data", RowsRemaining = n0, RowsRemoved = 0)

# 1. Missing CustomerID (cannot build customer-level features)
p <- nrow(df); df <- df %>% filter(!is.na(CustomerID)); steps[[2]] <- log_step(df, "Drop missing CustomerID", p)
# 2. Cancellations (invoice starts with 'C')
p <- nrow(df); df <- df %>% filter(!grepl("^C", InvoiceNo)); steps[[3]] <- log_step(df, "Drop cancelled invoices", p)
# 3. Non-positive quantity or price (returns, adjustments, free items)
p <- nrow(df); df <- df %>% filter(Quantity > 0, UnitPrice > 0); steps[[4]] <- log_step(df, "Drop Quantity<=0 / UnitPrice<=0", p)
# 4. Non-product stock codes (postage, manual, bank charges, ...)
p <- nrow(df); df <- df %>% filter(!grepl("^(POST|DOT|M|D|S|B|C2|BANK CHARGES|CRUK|PADS|AMAZONFEE)$", StockCode, ignore.case = TRUE))
steps[[5]] <- log_step(df, "Drop non-product StockCodes", p)
# 5. Exact duplicate rows
p <- nrow(df); df <- df %>% distinct(); steps[[6]] <- log_step(df, "Drop duplicate rows", p)

df <- df %>% mutate(CustomerID = as.character(CustomerID), Revenue = Quantity * UnitPrice)
cleaning_log <- bind_rows(steps); cleaning_log
write.csv(cleaning_log, "outputs/tables/cleaning_log.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("Unique customers after cleaning:", n_distinct(df$CustomerID), "\n")
```

# Customer-Level Feature Engineering

| Feature | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Recency** | Days since the customer's last purchase (relative to snapshot = last date + 1 day) |
| **Frequency** | Number of distinct invoices |
| **Monetary** | Total spend (Quantity x UnitPrice) |
| **AvgTxnValue** | Monetary / Frequency |
| **TotalQty** | Total units purchased |
| **PurchaseRate** | Invoices per month of customer lifetime (purchase frequency over time) |

```{r features}
snapshot <- max(df$InvoiceDate) + days(1)

cust <- df %>%
  group_by(CustomerID) %>%
  summarise(
    Recency      = as.numeric(difftime(snapshot, max(InvoiceDate), units = "days")),
    Frequency    = n_distinct(InvoiceNo),
    Monetary     = sum(Revenue),
    TotalQty     = sum(Quantity),
    FirstPurchase = min(InvoiceDate),
    LastPurchase  = max(InvoiceDate),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(AvgTxnValue = Monetary / Frequency,
         TenureMonths = pmax(as.numeric(difftime(LastPurchase, FirstPurchase, units = "days")) / 30.44, 1),
         PurchaseRate = Frequency / TenureMonths) %>%
  select(CustomerID, Recency, Frequency, Monetary, AvgTxnValue, TotalQty, PurchaseRate)

feat_cols <- c("Recency", "Frequency", "Monetary", "AvgTxnValue", "TotalQty", "PurchaseRate")
cat("Customers:", nrow(cust), "\n"); head(cust); summary(cust[, feat_cols])
write.csv(cust, "outputs/tables/customer_features_raw.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

## Distribution, Skewness and Outliers

```{r skew}
long <- cust %>% select(all_of(feat_cols)) %>% pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Feature", values_to = "Value")
p1 <- ggplot(long, aes(Value)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~Feature, scales = "free") + labs(title = "Raw feature distributions (heavily right-skewed)")
p1; save_fig(p1, "01_raw_distributions.png", 10, 6)
```

**Outlier and scaling strategy**

1. `log1p()` transform to reduce the heavy right skew typical of spend and frequency data.
2. **Winsorise** at the 1st and 99th percentiles to cap extreme outliers (rather than deleting genuine big spenders).
3. **Standardise** (z-score) so that K-Means / hierarchical clustering / SVM are not dominated by features with large units.

```{r scaling}
winsor <- function(x, lo = 0.01, hi = 0.99) { q <- quantile(x, c(lo, hi)); pmin(pmax(x, q[1]), q[2]) }

X_log    <- cust %>% select(all_of(feat_cols)) %>% mutate(across(everything(), log1p))
X_clean  <- X_log %>% mutate(across(everything(), winsor))
X_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(X_clean))
rownames(X_scaled) <- cust$CustomerID

long2 <- X_scaled %>% pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Feature", values_to = "Value")
p2 <- ggplot(long2, aes(Value)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "darkorange") +
  facet_wrap(~Feature, scales = "free") + labs(title = "After log1p + winsorisation + standardisation")
p2; save_fig(p2, "02_scaled_distributions.png", 10, 6)

cor_m <- round(cor(X_scaled), 2); cor_m
```

# K-Means Clustering

## Elbow Method

```{r elbow}
ks <- 1:10
wss <- sapply(ks, function(k) kmeans(X_scaled, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)$tot.withinss)
elbow_df <- data.frame(k = ks, WSS = wss)
p3 <- ggplot(elbow_df, aes(k, WSS)) + geom_line(colour = "steelblue") + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = ks) +
  labs(title = "Elbow Method: Total Within-Cluster Sum of Squares", x = "Number of clusters k", y = "WSS")
p3; save_fig(p3, "03_elbow_method.png")
```

## Silhouette Analysis to Confirm k

The elbow is often subjective, so average silhouette widths are also computed. A silhouette of k = 2 frequently wins on retail data (a "big" vs "small" split), but is too coarse for marketing, so the choice is restricted to **k between 3 and 6**.

```{r silhouette-k}
d <- dist(X_scaled)                       # Euclidean distance matrix (reused below)
sil_k <- sapply(2:8, function(k) {
  cl <- kmeans(X_scaled, centers = k, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)$cluster
  mean(silhouette(cl, d)[, 3])
})
sil_df <- data.frame(k = 2:8, AvgSilhouette = sil_k); sil_df
p4 <- ggplot(sil_df, aes(k, AvgSilhouette)) + geom_line(colour = "firebrick") + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "firebrick") +
  labs(title = "Average Silhouette Width by k", y = "Average silhouette")
p4; save_fig(p4, "04_silhouette_by_k.png")

K_OVERRIDE <- NULL                        # set e.g. K_OVERRIDE <- 4 to force a value after reading the elbow plot
K <- if (!is.null(K_OVERRIDE)) K_OVERRIDE else sil_df$k[sil_df$k %in% 3:6][which.max(sil_df$AvgSilhouette[sil_df$k %in% 3:6])]
cat("Selected number of clusters K =", K, "\n")
```

## Final K-Means Model

```{r kmeans}
km <- kmeans(X_scaled, centers = K, nstart = 50, iter.max = 200)
cust$KMeans <- km$cluster
table(cust$KMeans)
sil_km <- silhouette(km$cluster, d)
cat("K-Means average silhouette:", round(mean(sil_km[, 3]), 4), "\n")
```

# Hierarchical Clustering and Dendrogram

Ward's method (`ward.D2`) on the same standardised features.

```{r hclust, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
hc <- hclust(d, method = "ward.D2")
cust$Hier <- cutree(hc, k = K)

plot_dendro <- function() {
  plot(hc, labels = FALSE, hang = -1, main = paste("Dendrogram (Ward.D2) cut at k =", K),
       xlab = "Customers", sub = "")
  rect.hclust(hc, k = K, border = 2:(K + 1))
}
plot_dendro()
png("outputs/figures/05_dendrogram.png", width = 1400, height = 800, res = 130); plot_dendro(); invisible(dev.off())

sil_hc <- silhouette(cust$Hier, d)
cat("Hierarchical average silhouette:", round(mean(sil_hc[, 3]), 4), "\n")
table(cust$Hier)
```

## K-Means vs Hierarchical Comparison

```{r compare}
ari <- function(a, b) {
  tab <- table(a, b); n <- sum(tab); sc <- function(x) sum(choose(x, 2))
  sij <- sc(tab); sa <- sc(rowSums(tab)); sb <- sc(colSums(tab)); e <- sa * sb / choose(n, 2)
  (sij - e) / (0.5 * (sa + sb) - e)
}
comparison <- data.frame(
  Method = c("K-Means", "Hierarchical (Ward.D2)"),
  K = K,
  AvgSilhouette = c(mean(sil_km[, 3]), mean(sil_hc[, 3])),
  Smallest_cluster = c(min(table(cust$KMeans)), min(table(cust$Hier))),
  Largest_cluster  = c(max(table(cust$KMeans)), max(table(cust$Hier))))
comparison
cat("Adjusted Rand Index between the two partitions:", round(ari(cust$KMeans, cust$Hier), 4),
    " (1 = identical, 0 = random agreement)\n")
table(KMeans = cust$KMeans, Hierarchical = cust$Hier)
write.csv(comparison, "outputs/tables/clustering_comparison.csv", row.names = FALSE)

sil_plot_df <- data.frame(cluster = factor(sil_km[, 1]), width = sil_km[, 3]) %>% arrange(cluster, desc(width)) %>% mutate(i = row_number())
p5 <- ggplot(sil_plot_df, aes(i, width, fill = cluster)) + geom_col(width = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(sil_km[, 3]), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "K-Means silhouette plot", x = "Customers", y = "Silhouette width") + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
p5; save_fig(p5, "06_kmeans_silhouette_plot.png")
```

**Interpretation.** K-Means is used for the downstream work, as it scales better and gives compact clusters. The hierarchical solution acts as a cross-check: an Adjusted Rand Index well above 0 together with similar silhouette values indicates the segment structure is real and not an artefact of one algorithm.

# PCA Visualisation

```{r pca}
pca <- prcomp(X_scaled, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)   # data already standardised
var_exp <- summary(pca)$importance[2, ]
data.frame(PC = names(var_exp), VarianceExplained = round(var_exp * 100, 2), Cumulative = round(cumsum(var_exp) * 100, 2))
scree <- data.frame(PC = factor(names(var_exp), levels = names(var_exp)), Var = var_exp * 100)
p6 <- ggplot(scree, aes(PC, Var)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + geom_line(aes(group = 1)) + geom_point() +
  labs(title = "PCA scree plot", y = "% variance explained")
p6; save_fig(p6, "07_pca_scree.png")

round(pca$rotation[, 1:3], 3)   # loadings

pcs <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:3]); pcs$Cluster <- factor(cust$KMeans)
p7 <- ggplot(pcs, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = Cluster)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.4) +
  stat_ellipse(level = 0.9, linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Customer segments: 2D PCA projection",
       x = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", var_exp[1] * 100), y = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", var_exp[2] * 100))
p7; save_fig(p7, "08_pca_2d_clusters.png")
```

# Cluster Profiling

```{r profiling}
raw_prof <- cust %>% group_by(KMeans) %>%
  summarise(Customers = n(), Pct = round(100 * n() / nrow(cust), 1),
            Recency = mean(Recency), Frequency = mean(Frequency), Monetary = mean(Monetary),
            AvgTxnValue = mean(AvgTxnValue), TotalQty = mean(TotalQty), PurchaseRate = mean(PurchaseRate),
            Revenue_Share_Pct = 0, .groups = "drop")
raw_prof$Revenue_Share_Pct <- round(100 * tapply(cust$Monetary, cust$KMeans, sum) / sum(cust$Monetary), 1)

# Rank clusters: high Frequency + Monetary, low Recency = better
score <- rank(raw_prof$Frequency) + rank(raw_prof$Monetary) - rank(raw_prof$Recency)
ord <- order(score, decreasing = TRUE)
label_sets <- list(
  `2` = c("High-Value Loyalists", "Low-Value / Lapsed"),
  `3` = c("Champions", "Regular / Potential Loyalists", "Lost / Dormant"),
  `4` = c("Champions", "Loyal Customers", "At-Risk / Occasional", "Lost / Dormant"),
  `5` = c("Champions", "Loyal Customers", "Potential Loyalists", "At-Risk", "Lost / Dormant"),
  `6` = c("Champions", "Loyal Customers", "Potential Loyalists", "Occasional Buyers", "At-Risk", "Lost / Dormant"))
labs_k <- if (as.character(K) %in% names(label_sets)) label_sets[[as.character(K)]] else paste("Segment", seq_len(K))
raw_prof$Segment <- NA_character_; raw_prof$Segment[ord] <- labs_k
cust$Segment <- raw_prof$Segment[match(cust$KMeans, raw_prof$KMeans)]

profile_tbl <- raw_prof %>% arrange(match(Segment, labs_k)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Recency, Frequency, Monetary, AvgTxnValue, TotalQty, PurchaseRate), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  select(Segment, KMeans, Customers, Pct, Recency, Frequency, Monetary, AvgTxnValue, TotalQty, PurchaseRate, Revenue_Share_Pct)
knitr::kable(profile_tbl, caption = "Cluster profiles (means of the original, un-scaled features)")
write.csv(profile_tbl, "outputs/tables/cluster_profiles.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

> Segment names are assigned automatically from the ranking of Recency, Frequency and Monetary. Always sanity-check them against the table above before writing your final interpretation.

```{r profile-plots, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
prof_long <- cust %>% group_by(Segment) %>% summarise(across(all_of(feat_cols), mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Segment, names_to = "Feature", values_to = "Mean")
p8 <- ggplot(prof_long, aes(Segment, Mean, fill = Segment)) + geom_col() + facet_wrap(~Feature, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Mean feature values by segment") + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
p8; save_fig(p8, "09_segment_profiles.png", 10, 6)

rev_df <- profile_tbl %>% select(Segment, Pct, Revenue_Share_Pct) %>% pivot_longer(-Segment, names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Percent")
p9 <- ggplot(rev_df, aes(Segment, Percent, fill = Metric)) + geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Share of customers vs share of revenue", y = "%") + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
p9; save_fig(p9, "10_customer_vs_revenue_share.png")
```

# Predicting High-Value Customers (Supervised Learning)

## Target definition

The **high-value segment** is the top-ranked cluster (best combination of high frequency, high monetary value and low recency).

```{r target}
hv_cluster <- raw_prof$KMeans[ord[1]]
cust$HighValue <- factor(ifelse(cust$KMeans == hv_cluster, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
cat("High-value segment:", raw_prof$Segment[ord[1]], "(cluster", hv_cluster, ")\n")
table(cust$HighValue); round(prop.table(table(cust$HighValue)) * 100, 1)
```

## Train/test split (70/30, stratified)

```{r split}
set.seed(123)
idx_yes <- which(cust$HighValue == "Yes"); idx_no <- which(cust$HighValue == "No")
train_idx <- c(sample(idx_yes, round(0.7 * length(idx_yes))), sample(idx_no, round(0.7 * length(idx_no))))
model_df <- cbind(X_scaled, HighValue = cust$HighValue)
train <- model_df[train_idx, ]; test <- model_df[-train_idx, ]
cat("Train:", nrow(train), " Test:", nrow(test), "\n")
```

## Model training and evaluation

```{r models}
metrics <- function(truth, pred, prob, name) {
  cm <- table(Predicted = factor(pred, levels = c("No", "Yes")), Actual = truth)
  TP <- cm["Yes", "Yes"]; TN <- cm["No", "No"]; FP <- cm["Yes", "No"]; FN <- cm["No", "Yes"]
  prec <- TP / (TP + FP); rec <- TP / (TP + FN)
  list(cm = cm, roc = roc(truth, prob, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE),
       row = data.frame(Model = name, Accuracy = (TP + TN) / sum(cm), Precision = prec, Recall = rec,
                        F1 = 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec),
                        AUC = as.numeric(auc(roc(truth, prob, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)))))
}

fit_models <- function(train, test, label = "") {
  # Random Forest
  rf <- randomForest(HighValue ~ ., data = train, ntree = 500, importance = TRUE)
  rf_p <- predict(rf, test, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]; rf_c <- factor(ifelse(rf_p >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  # SVM (RBF) with 3-fold CV grid search
  tun <- tune(svm, HighValue ~ ., data = train, kernel = "radial", probability = TRUE,
              ranges = list(cost = c(0.5, 1, 5, 10), gamma = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.5)),
              tunecontrol = tune.control(cross = 3))
  sv <- tun$best.model
  sv_p <- attr(predict(sv, test, probability = TRUE), "probabilities")[, "Yes"]
  sv_c <- factor(ifelse(sv_p >= 0.5, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  list(rf = rf, svm = sv, tuned = tun,
       rf_m  = metrics(test$HighValue, rf_c, rf_p, paste0("Random Forest", label)),
       svm_m = metrics(test$HighValue, sv_c, sv_p, paste0("SVM (RBF)", label)))
}

res <- fit_models(train, test)
cat("Best SVM parameters: cost =", res$tuned$best.parameters$cost, " gamma =", res$tuned$best.parameters$gamma, "\n")
perf <- bind_rows(res$rf_m$row, res$svm_m$row) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
knitr::kable(perf, caption = "Test-set performance")
write.csv(perf, "outputs/tables/model_performance.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Confusion matrices

```{r cm}
cat("Random Forest\n"); print(res$rf_m$cm)
cat("\nSVM (RBF)\n");    print(res$svm_m$cm)

cm_df <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(res$rf_m$cm) %>% mutate(Model = "Random Forest"),
  as.data.frame(res$svm_m$cm) %>% mutate(Model = "SVM (RBF)"))
p10 <- ggplot(cm_df, aes(Actual, Predicted, fill = Freq)) + geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 6) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") + facet_wrap(~Model) + labs(title = "Confusion matrices (test set)")
p10; save_fig(p10, "11_confusion_matrices.png", 9, 4.5)
```

### ROC curves

```{r roc}
roc_df <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(FPR = 1 - res$rf_m$roc$specificities,  TPR = res$rf_m$roc$sensitivities,  Model = sprintf("Random Forest (AUC=%.3f)", res$rf_m$row$AUC)),
  data.frame(FPR = 1 - res$svm_m$roc$specificities, TPR = res$svm_m$roc$sensitivities, Model = sprintf("SVM (AUC=%.3f)", res$svm_m$row$AUC)))
p11 <- ggplot(roc_df, aes(FPR, TPR, colour = Model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "ROC curves (test set)", x = "False positive rate", y = "True positive rate")
p11; save_fig(p11, "12_roc_curves.png")
```

## Feature Importance (Random Forest)

```{r importance}
imp <- as.data.frame(importance(res$rf)); imp$Feature <- rownames(imp)
imp_long <- imp %>% select(Feature, MeanDecreaseGini, MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Feature, names_to = "Measure", values_to = "Importance")
p12 <- ggplot(imp_long, aes(reorder(Feature, Importance), Importance)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~Measure, scales = "free_x") + labs(title = "Random Forest feature importance", x = NULL)
p12; save_fig(p12, "13_feature_importance.png", 9, 4.5)
imp %>% arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseGini)) %>% select(Feature, MeanDecreaseGini, MeanDecreaseAccuracy) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## Leakage check (sensitivity analysis)

The target is defined from clusters that were **built from these very features**, so high accuracy is partly expected (the classifier is, in effect, re-learning the clustering rule). To see how much signal remains without the features that define "value" most directly, the models are refitted without `Monetary` and `AvgTxnValue`.

```{r leakage}
drop_cols <- c("Monetary", "AvgTxnValue")
res2 <- fit_models(train[, !(names(train) %in% drop_cols)], test[, !(names(test) %in% drop_cols)], label = " (no Monetary/AvgTxnValue)")
perf2 <- bind_rows(res$rf_m$row, res$svm_m$row, res2$rf_m$row, res2$svm_m$row) %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))
knitr::kable(perf2, caption = "Full feature set vs. leakage-aware feature set")
write.csv(perf2, "outputs/tables/model_performance_leakage_check.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Segment-wise Marketing Recommendations

```{r marketing}
recs <- data.frame(
  Segment = c("Champions", "High-Value Loyalists", "Loyal Customers", "Regular / Potential Loyalists", "Potential Loyalists",
              "Occasional Buyers", "At-Risk / Occasional", "At-Risk", "Lost / Dormant", "Low-Value / Lapsed"),
  Strategy = c(
    "VIP / early-access programme, exclusive bundles, referral rewards, personal thank-you. Do not over-discount: protect margin.",
    "VIP tier, early access, referral and loyalty rewards. Protect margin; reward behaviour instead of discounting.",
    "Loyalty points, cross-sell and up-sell of complementary products, subscription or replenishment reminders, product reviews.",
    "Nudge to a higher purchase frequency: tiered loyalty, 'spend X, get Y' thresholds, personalised recommendations.",
    "Onboarding journeys, second and third purchase incentives, category cross-sell, free-shipping thresholds.",
    "Seasonal and occasion-based campaigns (gifting peaks), bundles to lift basket size, newsletter engagement.",
    "Win-back emails with time-limited offers, 'we miss you' messages, survey to find why activity dropped.",
    "Win-back emails with time-limited offers, personalised reminders of past purchases, survey to understand churn reasons.",
    "Low-cost reactivation only (email / retargeting). Deep one-off discount as last attempt, then suppress to save spend.",
    "Low-cost automated nurture, entry-level bundles, clearance promotions; avoid expensive channels."),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
seg_recs <- recs %>% filter(Segment %in% cust$Segment) %>% mutate(o = match(Segment, labs_k)) %>% arrange(o) %>% select(-o)
if (nrow(seg_recs) < K) seg_recs <- data.frame(Segment = labs_k, Strategy = "Review profile table and design an offer accordingly.")
knitr::kable(seg_recs)
write.csv(seg_recs, "outputs/tables/marketing_recommendations.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Interpretation and Conclusion

```{r conclusion-numbers, echo=FALSE}
best_model <- perf$Model[which.max(perf$AUC)]
hv_row <- profile_tbl[1, ]
```

* **Segmentation.** K-Means with K = **`r K`** (chosen using the elbow plot and the average silhouette) gives an average silhouette of **`r round(mean(sil_km[,3]), 3)`**; Ward hierarchical clustering gives **`r round(mean(sil_hc[,3]), 3)`**, with an Adjusted Rand Index of **`r round(ari(cust$KMeans, cust$Hier), 3)`** between the two partitions.
* **PCA.** The first two components capture **`r round(sum(var_exp[1:2]) * 100, 1)`%** of the variance; the first three capture **`r round(sum(var_exp[1:3]) * 100, 1)`%**. The 2D and 3D projections show how the segments separate.
* **High-value segment.** The "`r hv_row$Segment`" segment makes up **`r hv_row$Pct`%** of customers but contributes **`r hv_row$Revenue_Share_Pct`%** of revenue (Pareto-style concentration), so retaining it is the top commercial priority.
* **Prediction.** On the held-out test set the better model by ROC-AUC is **`r best_model`** (see the performance table). Feature importance shows which behaviours separate high-value customers from the rest.
* **Caveat.** Because the target comes from clusters built on the same features, the supervised scores are optimistic. The leakage check above shows how much predictive power remains without the directly value-defining variables.
* **Business action.** Apply the segment-specific strategies above: reward and retain the top segment, grow the middle, win back at-risk customers cheaply, and stop spending on dormant ones.

**Limitations and future work:** only about a year of data; no product or category features; RFM is a snapshot, so a temporal split (features from the first months, labels from later months) would give a leakage-free churn / CLV prediction model.
